notice: Every value that drives the baggage scenarios is listed here with its tier and source. REAL_PUBLIC and BENCHMARK values are published facts; ASSUMPTION values are team-set and are not figures of any named airline, handler or airport. Operational records generated from these values are SYNTHETIC.

bag_drop_cutoff_min.used_for: Latest time a local bag is accepted before departure (international)
bag_drop_cutoff_min.source: Thai Airways check-in policy: checked baggage should be dropped at least 60 minutes before the flight; international counters close 50 minutes before departure

tracking_points.used_for: Stages where a scan is mandatory; screening and sorting scans are BHS/BRS extras
tracking_points.source: IATA Resolution 753: passenger handover to airline, loading onto the aircraft, delivery to the transfer area, return to the passenger

avg_passengers_per_movement.source: Suvarnabhumi fiscal year 2025: 62.9 million passengers / 370,823 aircraft movements, as reported from AOT figures. Check against the AOT Annual Report 2025 before citing on a slide.

transfer_share_of_mishandling_pct.used_for: Why transfer bags are ranked first; not used as a simulation input
transfer_share_of_mishandling_pct.source: SITA Baggage IT Insights 2026 (2025 data): transfers caused 39% of mishandling; 4.9 mishandled bags per 1,000 passengers; USD 260 average cost per bag

bags_per_passenger.used_for: Checked bags per passenger on a synthetic international departure
bags_per_passenger.source: Team assumption; no public figure for BKK found

transfer_bag_share.used_for: Share of a flight's bags that arrive from an inbound connection
transfer_bag_share.source: Team assumption; requires an airline connection feed to replace

departures_in_window.used_for: Departures served by one handler in the four-hour scenario window
departures_in_window.source: Team assumption. Scale check only: BKK averaged about 1,016 movements a day in fiscal year 2025, roughly 21 departures an hour across all handlers

normal_capacity_headroom.used_for: Normal stage capacity as a multiple of planned demand: busiest five minutes for automated stages, busiest hour for manual stages
normal_capacity_headroom.source: Team assumption; to be replaced by measured BRS throughput

load_close_before_departure_min.used_for: Hold closes this many minutes before departure; later bags miss the flight
load_close_before_departure_min.source: Team assumption; confirm with a ground-handling expert

flood_staff_ratio.used_for: Share of planned manual loading capacity available in the flood scenario
flood_staff_ratio.source: Team assumption. The real incident reported staff unable to reach work and faulty baggage vehicles but published no ratio

stage_wait_thresholds_min.used_for: Age of the oldest bag still waiting at screening, sorting or loading that turns the stage from OK to WATCH to DELAY
stage_wait_thresholds_min.source: Team assumption; confirm with a baggage operations controller

feed_stale_after_min.used_for: Bags are waiting at a stage but its newest scan is older than this: the stage has stopped or its feed is down, so it is shown as STALE and must be verified

inbound_wait_thresholds_min.used_for: Same thresholds for the transfer and arrival stages, where a whole aircraft load arrives at once
inbound_wait_thresholds_min.source: Team assumption; confirm against the handler's first-bag/last-bag service levels

min_transfer_minutes.used_for: Shortest time from inbound on-block to the connecting hold closing for a transfer bag to make it; shorter connections are flagged
min_transfer_minutes.source: Team assumption; replace with the airport's published minimum connecting time for baggage

risk_horizon_min.used_for: Flights whose hold closes within this time are checked for bags at risk; beyond it the projection is too uncertain

reference_incident.role: Shows that the causal chain is real. Not an input to the simulation and not a result of One TrustX.

facts.fact: CAAT NEWS 30/2569: continuous heavy rain and flooding disrupt road access to Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang; flights may be delayed or rescheduled
Flooding disrupted journeys to work for Thai Airways ground-handling staff; faulty baggage transport carts added to the shortage; departures delayed and arriving passengers waited longer for bags
131 military personnel deployed (100 Royal Thai Air Force, 31 Royal Thai Army)
Thai Airways CEO: about 5,000 bags from the airline's flights remained at Suvarnabhumi
More than 10,000 bags accumulated 26-29 Sept; about 1,800 returned; about 8,000 outstanding; clearing capacity about 2,000 bags a day; cargo acceptance suspended 30 Sept-6 Oct; flights reduced
1,092 bags remained, expected to clear by 4 Oct

rainfall_mm_per_day.source: Open-Meteo historical archive, grid point nearest BKK (13.6811, 100.7470); model reanalysis, not an airport rain gauge
